summary: Hungary is part of the EU and the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa costing €90.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

passportValidity.text: Non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen Area and have been issued within the last 10 years.

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it but border officers may ask about cover.

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. There is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorization System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal gives a duty-free allowance of 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine), and other goods worth up to €300 (€430 by air or sea). Hungary applies the EU's lower tobacco limit to travellers arriving by land or sea — 40 cigarettes instead of 200 — and travellers under 17 get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.
Between EU countries, alcohol and tobacco bought with tax paid, for your own use and not for resale, owe no further tax, according to the EU's Your Europe portal.

safety.text: Hungary is one of Europe's safest destinations. The main risks for visitors are pickpocketing on Budapest transport and around sights, and overcharging by unofficial taxis and some bars.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Hungary travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official seasonal guidance; the months shown are not an official recommendation. The CIA World Factbook describes Hungary's climate as temperate, with cold, cloudy, humid winters and warm summers.

roadVignette.appliesTo: Category D1 — cars with up to seven seats and their trailers; motorbikes (D1M) pay less, larger vehicles (D2) more.
roadVignette.text: Hungarian motorways are paid for with the e-matrica, an electronic vignette registered to the number plate. There is no sticker to display. Besides the national vignettes above there are cheaper annual county vignettes, worth comparing if your driving stays within one or two counties. Buy from the national toll operator or its resellers; the price is the same everywhere.

source.name: Hungarian Public Roads Nonprofit PLC, Toll Division — E-vignette rates

idp.text: Hungary is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: Hungary is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Hungary yet.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Hungary — days spent in Austria or Slovakia count against the same allowance.

Pay in forint (HUF). Canada's travel advice says euros are accepted only in Budapest and some other major cities where a sign is posted, often at uncompetitive rates, and warns against unofficial moneychangers.

In Hungary, Canada's travel advice says to use only officially marked taxis, to call one through a dispatcher rather than hailing it on the street, and to make sure the meter is on and shows the correct rate. It reports overcharging by taxi drivers, and that some drivers take part in bar and restaurant bill scams, so do not ask them to recommend bars or clubs.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Hungary?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Hungary and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Hungary Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries, and applications are decided within 15–45 calendar days.

faq.question: Does Hungary use the euro?
faq.answer: No. Hungary uses the Hungarian forint (HUF). Canada's travel advice says euros are accepted in Budapest and some other major cities where a sign is posted, but that the rates may not be competitive.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Hungary?
faq.answer: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once mandatory, the €20 online authorization will be required before boarding. Check the official EU website for the current status.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Hungary without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area. EU and EFTA citizens can stay indefinitely but must register locally after 3 months.
